strongest_angle: In 1963, 17-year-old orphan Elizabeth Tyler documented the bomb sites of Coventry using a 1933 Rolleicord camera, creating an archive rediscovered six decades later.

key_facts.fact: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler wandered the streets of Coventry capturing images of the city's bomb sites and abandoned buildings.
Elizabeth Tyler bought a Rolleicord camera from 1933 using her first wages from an evening job as a waitress while enrolled at the Coventry College of Art.
The published book of Elizabeth Tyler's 1960s Coventry archive contains 36 pages printed in England with staple binding.

quotes.text: The environment was certainly harsh, reeking of poverty and hopelessness, but there is a defiant glint in the eyes of Tyler's subjects that belies that impression
